title: Sumathi Holdings celebrates 70 years of success | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 27 October 2026 01:54
-     - 648

Sumathi Holdings marked its 70th anniversary on 9 October, with a celebration at the Sangam Ballroom of ITC Ratnadipa, Colombo, attended by over 500 guests from Sri Lanka’s business, government, financial and media communities. 

Held under the theme “70 Years of Sumathi Legacy”, the evening looked back to 1956, when founder Mr. U.W. Sumathipala opened Sporting Star’s first betting shop on Maliban Street, Pettah – the business from which the Group grew.

The evening opened with a drone show and fireworks over Galle Face. The program that followed included an address and toast by Chairman Jagath Sumathipala, the unveiling of the 70th anniversary logo, and addresses by Directors Chadu Sumathipala and Chathula Sumathipala, accompanied by a live orchestra and performances by vocalist Umara Sinhawansa, pianist and music director Soundarie David Rodrigo, and composer and singer Nadeeka Guruge.

U.W. Sumathipala built Sporting Star into one of the country’s leading bookmakers and established it as the market leader. He also expanded into cinema, supporting the growth of the Sri Lankan film industry and into gems, representing the business at The World Gem and Jewellery Exhibition in Milan. His values of “Honesty and Integrity” remain the Group’s guiding principles today.

After U.W. Sumathipala’s passing in 1979, Jagath Sumathipala joined the business at the age of 19, supported by his maternal uncle, Dharmasiri, who guided him in the horse racing operations. His first assignment was to create the Group’s own race paper, which he turned into a commercial printing company. He moved the main office from Maliban Street to Chatham Street and carried forward his father’s gem business. When his brother, Thilanga Sumathipala, returned from his studies in 1986, Jagath Sumathipala handed the racing operations over to him, and Thilanga Sumathipala built them further.

In 1987 took a new step, Jagath Sumathipala opened Sri Lanka’s first race-by-race live commentary betting shop. Building on this, the Group began broadcasting races in 1992 and by 1998 was showing every race live across all its outlets. Today Sporting Star operates more than 200 outlets across the island and, since 2019, the online platform BetSS.com.

Milina Sumathipala’s influence reached well beyond the business. She gave the entire profit of her film Ganga Addara (1980) to build a Neurosurgery Unit at the Colombo General Hospital, today’s National Hospital. In 1981, she began the blood donation drives and support for the Cancer Hospital through which more than 20,000 pints of blood have since been donated, and in 2001 she became the first woman President of the All Ceylon Buddhist Congress.

Following a restructuring in 2017, Jagath Sumathipala, together with the third generation, has shaped Sumathi Holdings into a Group of 11 principal businesses employing more than 2,000 people, across betting and gaming, healthcare, information technology, restaurants, security, printing, renewable energy, investments and film.

Much of today’s Group began as an answer to something Sporting Star needed. Security for its outlets became Lokx Security Services; printing for its racing papers became InPrint Solutions; and the technology behind its betting systems is now developed by Mainframe.

Three Group companies mark milestones of their own this year:

Great Wall Restaurants turns 35. Jagath Sumathipala set it up in 1991 on Chatham Street to bring authentic Chinese food to Colombo.

Sumathi IT turns 25. It provides network infrastructure, data communications and geospatial engineering across Sri Lanka, and introduced DJI’s enterprise drones to the country.

LifeServ turns 25. The healthcare distributor has been a leader in Sri Lanka’s drug-eluting stent market for two decades and opened an oncology division in 2025.

A third generation now leads the Group alongside the Chairman. Chadu Sumathipala leads the Group’s IT sector: he founded Mainframe, brought the Group’s key systems in-house, built BetSS.com, and set up Sumathi IT’s drone division and its first research and development centre. Chathula Sumathipala leads the Group’s services cluster and grew LifeServ built Sumathi Energy, whose projects include the 5MW Wewila solar plant and battery storage at Monaragala and Wewila.

The celebrations extended to the Group’s people. On 8 October, Sporting Star’s head office celebrated with its staff and presented long-service awards to more than 200 employees with ten or more years’ service, 31 of whom have been with the company for over 30 years. The longest-serving, R.V. Ghanasena of Anuradhapura, has been with Sporting Star for 40 years. On 10 October, Sporting Star outlets across the island held celebrations of their own for staff from Great Wall Restaurants and commemorative gifts for customers.

Sumathi Holdings Chairman Jagath Sumathipala said: “Seventy years ago, my father opened a single shop on Maliban Street, built on his word and the trust of his customers. Honesty and integrity built this Group, and the more than 2,000 people who stand with us today carry those values forward. As we enter our eighth decade, our commitment is to build the businesses that will serve Sri Lanka for the next seventy years.”

title: OPA presents collective professional proposals for Budget 2027 | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 27 October 2026 01:53
-     - 315

The Organisation of Professional Associations of Sri Lanka (OPA), under the leadership of OPA President Jayantha Gallehewa, presented its proposals and recommendations for the Budget 2027 to Treasury Secretary Dr. Harshana Suriyapperuma at a meeting held on 6 October, 2026.

The proposals represent the collective voice and professional expertise of the OPA’s 52 member associations, bringing together knowledge and perspectives from across Sri Lanka’s professional community. The initiative was undertaken through the National Issues Committee (NIC), chaired by OPA Vice President and NIC Chairman Bhanu Wijayaratne, with the active contribution of its members.

The proposals were developed through consultations with the OPA’s member associations and focused on key areas of national importance, with the objective of providing constructive and evidence-informed recommendations to the national Budget process.

Among the key areas addressed were fair taxation, export financing, elder care and social protection, research and innovation, the circular economy, the built environment and heritage, and measures to address the country’s professional brain drain. The proposals also reflected wider professional perspectives on strengthening economic resilience, improving productivity, encouraging investment and supporting sustainable national development.

The OPA delegation was led by OPA President Jayantha Gallehewa and included General Secretary Eng. Ravi Rupasinghe, Vice President and NIC Chairman Bhanu Wijayaratne, NIC Member B.A.H.S. Preena, OPA Assistant Secretary Indika Ranaweera, Vice President and Career Guidance and Skills Development Committee Chairman V. Rameshkumar, NIC Member and Career Guidance and Skills Development Committee Convener Udesh I.W. Seneviratna and OPA Editor Priyantha Wickramarathna.

Speaking on the occasion, Gallehewa emphasised the organisation’s commitment to placing the knowledge, experience and collective expertise of Sri Lanka’s professional community at the service of the nation. He noted that the OPA’s role extends beyond representing individual professions and includes contributing constructively to national policy and decision-making.

The presentation of the Budget proposals marks another important step in the OPA’s continuing engagement with the Government. Through the NIC and its 52 member associations, the OPA continues to provide a platform for translating professional knowledge and experience into practical recommendations on matters of national importance.

The OPA expressed its appreciation to the Finance, Planning and Economic Development Ministry for providing the opportunity to present its proposals and reaffirmed its readiness to continue contributing professional expertise to the national development and Budget process.

title: Corrugated carton industry under growing cost pressure | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 27 October 2026 00:00
-     - 218

Sri Lanka’s corrugated carton industry is facing mounting financial pressure as the cost of paper and other essential inputs continues to rise. For many manufacturers, the challenge is no longer simply maintaining profitability; it is ensuring the industry’s sustainability.

While several packaging sectors have adjusted their prices in response to rising costs, corrugated carton manufacturers initially took a more cautious approach. Many held prices steady, expecting global supply-chain disruptions, geopolitical tensions and commodity-price increases to ease. That relief has yet to arrive.

Instead, the prices of key paper grades used in carton production, including Kraft Liner, White Liner, Test Liner and Medium, have continued to climb by 30-50% across different paper grades. Manufacturers are also contending with higher costs for energy, transport, chemicals, starch, inks, labour, maintenance and other operating needs in line with growing inflation and global market realities. Together, these increases are placing the sector under severe strain.

Manufacturers have worked to absorb as much of the additional cost as possible while continuing to serve customers at competitive prices. They have reduced waste, improved machine efficiency, managed energy use, optimized transport and strengthened production productivity. These efforts have helped, but they cannot offset rising costs indefinitely.

Paper accounts for a substantial share of the cost of producing corrugated cartons. Even a modest increase in paper prices can significantly affect the final cost of a carton; when prices rise across all major grades, the cumulative impact is considerable. This leaves manufacturers caught between escalating costs and intense competition. Customers need affordable packaging, while producers must recover enough to maintain quality, invest in machinery, retain skilled employees and deliver reliably.

The consequences could extend well beyond the carton industry. Corrugated cartons are an essential part of Sri Lanka’s manufacturing and export supply chain. Food and beverage producers, tea exporters, agricultural businesses, apparel manufacturers, pharmaceutical companies and many others depend on a reliable supply of quality cartons.

If carton manufacturers face growing financial difficulties, the effects may spread across these industries. Higher packaging costs could also weaken Sri Lanka’s export competitiveness, particularly when local exporters are already competing with producers that may have better access to raw materials or lower production costs.

The sector is therefore calling for a realistic understanding of the pressures it faces. Manufacturers did not rush to raise prices when costs first began to rise. They waited, hoping conditions would improve and paper prices would return to more sustainable levels. Instead, the pressures have persisted.

A responsible adjustment to carton prices may now be necessary, not simply to improve margins, but to help ensure that manufacturers can continue operating sustainably. The challenge is to balance customers’ need to manage costs with the need for carton manufacturers to remain financially viable. The industry is not asking for an easy solution; it is asking for recognition of the realities facing the sector.

A sustainable corrugated carton industry is essential to Sri Lanka’s manufacturing and export sectors. Preserving it will require cooperation among paper suppliers, manufacturers, customers, exporters and policymakers. Without appropriate market adjustments, continued cost pressures could have consequences far beyond the carton industry itself.

title: Lankan pharmaceutical manufacturers gain global exposure at CPHI Worldwide 2026 in Milan | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 26 October 2026 07:03
-     - 359

The Sri Lanka Export Development Board (EDB), in collaboration with the Embassy of Sri Lanka in Rome and the Consulate General of Sri Lanka in Milan, facilitated an exposure visit for Sri Lankan pharmaceutical manufacturers to the 37th edition of CPHI Worldwide 2026, held from 6 to 8 October 2026 at Fiera Milano, Milan, Italy. 

The program also included dedicated business networking sessions in Milan for the pharmaceutical sector.

A five-member business delegation representing five Sri Lankan companies participated in the exposure visit to explore opportunities to strengthen the international market presence of Sri Lankan manufacturers.

The participating companies were State Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Corporation, Siddhalepa Exports Ltd., Lina Manufacturing Ltd., Vetpharma Biotechnology Ltd., and Aithra Pharmaceuticals Ltd,, representing the pharmaceutical, veterinary, cosmeceutical and natural products sectors. The program provided an opportunity to gain exposure to international markets, explore potential business partnerships and identify avenues for expanding Sri Lanka’s presence in global markets.

CPHI Worldwide is a major international platform connecting stakeholders across the pharmaceutical value chain, including pharmaceutical manufacturers, active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) suppliers, contract development and manufacturing organisations (CDMOs), packaging providers, and specialist technical service companies. The event provides opportunities to explore emerging market trends, establish business relationships, and identify potential areas for commercial and technical cooperation.

Participation in the event enabled the Sri Lankan delegation to gain exposure to international pharmaceutical industry developments, explore potential export markets, and identify opportunities for collaboration with international industry stakeholders.

The pharmaceutical industry operates within a highly regulated environment, with manufacturers required to meet applicable product registration, quality, and regulatory requirements in both domestic and export markets. Obtaining market authorisation can be a lengthy and costly process, particularly in highly regulated markets where stringent manufacturing standards, including European Union Good Manufacturing Practice (EU-GMP) requirements, may apply.

Despite these developments, the sector continues to face challenges in keeping pace with evolving international market requirements, emerging products and technologies, regulatory frameworks, marketing strategies, new molecules, advanced manufacturing systems, and global pharmaceutical supply chains. Addressing these knowledge gaps is important to support the transition towards higher-value production and improved access to more regulated export markets.

Recognising these needs, the EDB facilitated the exposure visit to provide participating companies with opportunities to observe international industry developments, improve their understanding of global market expectations, and identify potential business and technology partnerships.

In addition to the exhibition visit, the Consulate General of Sri Lanka in Milan organised business networking sessions for the Sri Lankan delegation. These sessions provided participants with opportunities to engage with potential buyers, distributors, and other pharmaceutical industry stakeholders, explore prospective export markets, and discuss possible business collaborations.

The exposure visit to CPHI Worldwide 2026 enabled the Sri Lankan delegation to engage with international pharmaceutical companies and specialised service providers, including Barbados Pharmaceutical Inc. (Barbados), Orion GXP Consulting (Ireland), Gruppo Farmalpresa (Italy), Intertek (United Kingdom), Nanopharm (France) and NATAC (Spain), as well as representatives of the Ministry of Health of Tanzania. These engagements provided opportunities to explore potential business partnerships, technical cooperation, pharmaceutical product development, natural ingredients, regulatory requirements and international market development.

The EDB said it will continue to work with industry stakeholders and Sri Lanka’s overseas missions to promote Sri Lankan pharmaceutical products, facilitate international business linkages, and support the long-term development and competitiveness of the country’s pharmaceutical export sector.

title: Lankan envoy in Bangladesh meets Dhaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 26 October 2026 07:01
-     - 203

The High Commissioner of Sri Lanka to Bangladesh, Dharmapala Weerakkody, met with the Dhaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry (DCCI) President Taskeen Ahmed, on 18 October 2026 at the DCCI office in Gulshan, Dhaka, to explore avenues for strengthening economic, trade and investment cooperation between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.

The DCCI is a prominent private-sector business organisation in Bangladesh that represents businesses and entrepreneurs, particularly in Dhaka, and promotes trade, investment and industrial development through policy advocacy, business networking and public-private sector collaboration.

The discussions focused on enhancing bilateral trade and investment by creating opportunities for the business communities of both countries in pharmaceuticals, Information Technology (IT), renewable energy, logistics, tourism and other emerging sectors.

During the meeting, High Commissioner Weerakkody briefed the DCCI President on Sri Lanka Expo 2027, Sri Lanka’s premier international trade exhibition, scheduled to be held from 14 to 17 January 2027 at the Bandaranaike Memorial International Conference Hall (BMICH) in Colombo. He invited the DCCI to facilitate the participation of a business delegation at the exhibition, which will provide a platform for businesses from both countries to explore trade, investment and commercial partnerships.

The DCCI President welcomed the initiative and expressed a positive response to the proposed participation of a business delegation at Sri Lanka Expo 2027, highlighting the potential to strengthen business-to-business linkages and expand bilateral trade and investment.

Highlighting advances in the artificial intelligence (AI) sector in both countries, the DCCI President invited Sri Lanka to participate in the “Bangladesh AI Business Summit 2026”, organised by the DCCI in partnership with the Ministry of Science and Technology (MoST) of Bangladesh. The Summit is scheduled to be held on 5 November 2026 at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center (BCFCC) in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka.

The meeting also underscored the importance of strengthening direct engagement between the private sectors of Sri Lanka and Bangladesh and identifying new areas of collaboration to support sustained economic growth and closer bilateral relations.

The Second Secretary of the High Commission of Sri Lanka in Dhaka, Gayanga Dias, the DCCI Vice President Salem Sulaiman, and other senior DCCI officials were also present at the meeting.

title: Alumex wins Bronze at National AI Awards 2026 for AI-powered manufacturing innovation | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 26 October 2026 06:58
-     - 112

Representatives of Alumex PLC holding the award trophy and framed certificate at the National AI Awards 2026 after winning Bronze in the Best AI Solution in Manufacturing & Industry 5.0 category

Alumex PLC, a member of the Hayleys Group and a leading manufacturer of aluminium extrusions in Sri Lanka, has won a Bronze award in the ‘Best AI Solution in Manufacturing and Industry 5.0’ category at the National AI Awards 2026 on 30 September. The award was bestowed under the auspices of the Digital Economy Ministry.

The award-winning innovation is an extruder production monitoring system and smart real-time energy monitoring and analytics system, featuring an AI-powered golden batch for extrusion digitisation. This recognition acknowledges the company’s application of AI and data analytics to improve production monitoring alongside process consistency and energy management across its manufacturing operations. In addition, the solution provides real-time visibility into extrusion operations and production performance, while through its AI-powered golden batch, production data is analysed to identify process variations, improve batch consistency and support faster, data-driven decisions. The smart real-time energy monitoring and analytics system tracks energy consumption across the manufacturing process, helping identify opportunities to optimise energy use and improve operational efficiency.

The Bronze award marks a significant step in the company’s continued advancement in smart manufacturing, reflecting its focus on integrating digital capabilities into its operations and building more connected, responsive and technology-enabled manufacturing processes. Alumex PLC remains committed to exploring innovative applications of technology across its operations.

title: Cabinet awards Rs. 562 m wastewater plant contract for Welipenna Expressway Service Area to Water Board | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 26 October 2026 06:52
-     - 167

The Cabinet of Ministers has approved awarding the contract to construct two wastewater treatment plants for the Welipenna service area on the Southern Expressway to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB), at an estimated cost of Rs. 562.04 million.

The service area is maintained by Canowin Hotels and Spas Ltd., a fully owned subsidiary of the Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation. It has been identified that the capacity of the existing wastewater treatment plants at the facility is insufficient.

The NWSDB examined the prevailing conditions at the site and submitted a report recommending the construction of two new treatment plants, each with a capacity of 200 cubic metres per day.

The proposal to this effect was submitted by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in his capacity as the Finance, Planning and Economic Development Minister.

title: Cabinet clears drafting of Bill to amend Ayurveda Act | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 26 October 2026 06:52
-     - 69

The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the formulation of a draft Bill to amend the Ayurveda Act, No. 31 of 1961, which governs the regulation, development, and control of Sri Lanka’s indigenous medical sector.

The sector, which comprises Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani, and local therapies, is regulated under the Act. Although it has been amended from time to time as required, the need for further amendments has been identified.

The proposed changes are aimed at enabling all activities in the local medical field to be managed more efficiently and productively, and at further formalising the regulation of the sector. 

They would also allow for the issuing of licences applicable to the export of local medicines, and support progress towards Sustainable Development Goals in the sector.

The proposal to this effect was submitted by Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa.

title: Prof. Sarath Kodithuwakku: Legacy beyond lecture hall | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 24 October 2026 00:00
-     - 1157

Prof. Sarath S. Kodithuwakku

A memento being presented to Prof. Sivananthan of Sivananthan Laboratories Inc., USA in appreciation of its generous sponsorship to forge and sustain collaborations with the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC)

A memento being presented to former University of Illinois System Vice-Chancellor and President Prof. Robert Easter for the same purpose

As Prof. Sarath S. Kodithuwakku retires from the University of Peradeniya on 24 October, 2026, his distinguished career reflects a lasting contribution to academic innovation, institution building and the transformation of management and agricultural education in Sri Lanka.

The contribution of an academic is often measured through research publications, qualifications, administrative positions and years of service. Yet the true significance of an academic career is sometimes better reflected in the institutions established, the opportunities created and the generations of students whose lives have been influenced along the way.

Prof. Kodithuwakku represents this broader dimension of academic achievement.

Over more than three decades, his contributions have extended across agricultural education, business management, entrepreneurship, postgraduate studies, research and university administration. A defining characteristic of his career has been his willingness to challenge conventional academic boundaries and introduce initiatives that connect university education with the evolving needs of industry and society.

Redefining agricultural higher education

One of Prof. Kodithuwakku’s most significant contributions has been his role in broadening the traditional scope of agricultural education.

At a time when agricultural studies were predominantly associated with production and the sciences, he recognised the growing importance of integrating business management, marketing and entrepreneurship into agricultural education.

This thinking contributed to the evolution of the Department of Agricultural Economics into the Department of Agricultural Economics and Business Management at the University of Peradeniya, reflecting a more commercially oriented and multidisciplinary approach.

His contribution to curriculum development was equally important. As Chairman of the Curriculum Committee and subsequently as Dean of the Faculty of Agriculture, he played a leading role in initiating the revision of the BSc Honours in Agricultural Technology and Management degree program, which included the introduction of a major-minor structure that offered students greater academic flexibility.

He also pioneered an innovative approach to promoting agricultural higher education, introducing structured branding and marketing communication to reposition the degree and broaden public understanding of its professional opportunities.

These initiatives reflected his conviction that universities must continuously evolve to remain relevant to changing economic and professional realities.

Bringing management education beyond Colombo

Among his most enduring institutional achievements was the establishment of the Master of Business Administration (MBA) program at the Postgraduate Institute of Agriculture (PGIA), University of Peradeniya, in 1998.

It was the first MBA program offered outside Colombo and the third established by a Sri Lankan state university.

At a time when postgraduate management education was largely concentrated in the capital, this initiative marked an important step towards widening access to advanced management education.

As Founder Coordinator, Prof. Kodithuwakku played a central role in establishing and developing the program. He subsequently contributed to establishing the Board of Study in Business Administration and introduced the Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) program at PGIA in 2005, further extending the Institute’s contribution to postgraduate management education.

The MBA program has since provided opportunities for professionals, managers and entrepreneurs to advance their knowledge, while strengthening the connection between academic learning and organisational practice.

Its continuing relevance is an example of institution building whose influence extends far beyond the tenure of its founder.

Turning entrepreneurship into experience

Prof. Kodithuwakku’s approach to teaching was shaped by a fundamental belief: entrepreneurship cannot be adequately understood through theory alone.

This philosophy led to the introduction of Business Creation and Management, an undergraduate course that encouraged students to establish and operate real business ventures.

The initiative went beyond conventional classroom instruction, allowing students to experience the practical challenges of entrepreneurship, financial management and commercial decision-making.

Profits generated through these ventures were reinvested in student development, supporting participation in international academic conferences and sporting events. The student fund also enabled the establishment of four gold medals recognising excellence in Business Management and Agricultural Economics.

A similar philosophy underpinned The Kiosk, a student-managed restaurant developed with the support of the Faculty and its alumni. Beyond generating income for students, it served as a practical learning environment for developing entrepreneurial, business and managerial capabilities.

Together, these initiatives demonstrated how academic innovation could simultaneously strengthen education, entrepreneurship and student welfare.

A commitment to students that began early

An equally meaningful contribution began in 1990 when Prof. Kodithuwakku, then an undergraduate, joined his batchmates in establishing the Needy Students Scholarship Fund at the Faculty of Agriculture.

Conceived as a collective effort to assist financially disadvantaged students, the initiative gradually developed into an enduring tradition of student-supported fundraising.

Successive undergraduate batches sustained the 

program, which eventually became associated with the annual Indeewaree Musical Show.

The fund has since grown to approximately Rs. 15 million and continues to support students facing financial difficulties.

What makes this initiative particularly noteworthy is that it originated long before Prof. Kodithuwakku assumed any formal academic leadership position. It reflected an early understanding that higher education carries responsibilities extending beyond individual academic advancement.

Connecting universities with the wider economy

Prof. Kodithuwakku also played an important role in strengthening the relationship between university research and practical economic development.

His involvement with the Agribusiness Centre of the University of Peradeniya, dating back to its establishment in 1997, contributed to the development of an institutional platform connecting academic expertise with agricultural enterprises, industry and rural communities.

His research and consultancy work encompassed agricultural marketing, entrepreneurship, food security, value-chain development and smallholder livelihoods, involving collaborations with national and international development and research organisations.

His international academic experience included serving as an Assistant Professor at Sultan Qaboos University in Oman from 2011 to 2016, further enriching his contribution to teaching, research and institutional development.

More recently, he provided strategic leadership in initiating an international research collaboration involving Prof. Sivananthan of Sivananthan Laboratories Inc., USA, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC), the Faculty of Agriculture of the University of Peradeniya and Sri Lanka’s Department of Agriculture. The collaboration focuses on soybean varietal trials to strengthen domestic soybean production, while also fostering academic collaboration between the two universities to enhance agricultural education and research.

These engagements demonstrated his consistent interest in ensuring that universities contribute meaningfully to national development.

Leadership through challenging times

Prof. Kodithuwakku served as Dean of the Faculty of Agriculture from November 2021 to November 2024, during one of the most difficult periods experienced by Sri Lankan universities.

The aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic and the country’s economic crisis created unprecedented institutional and operational challenges.

Despite these pressures, his tenure saw continued attention to curriculum reform, academic development, institutional partnerships and student welfare.

His leadership experience also included four terms as Head of the Department of Agricultural Economics and Business Management and several appointments as Acting Vice-Chancellor of the University of Peradeniya.

Beyond academia, he contributed extensively to professional management education, including leadership of the Institute of Management of Sri Lanka and longstanding involvement with the Sri Lanka Institute of Marketing.

His role in advancing professional management education and recognition initiatives further strengthened the relationship between academia and Sri Lanka’s business community.

A legacy that will endure

Across his academic career, Prof. Kodithuwakku has supervised approximately 200 undergraduate dissertations and 100 MBA dissertations, alongside doctoral research mentorship, scholarly publications and numerous institutional responsibilities.

Yet perhaps his most significant contribution cannot be adequately expressed through these conventional measures.

The MBA program he established continues to educate professionals. The curriculum reforms he championed have broadened the possibilities available to agricultural graduates. His entrepreneurship initiatives have helped translate academic knowledge into practical experience, while the scholarship fund he helped establish as an undergraduate continues to support new generations of students.

These contributions share an important characteristic: their value extends beyond the individual who initiated them.

As Prof. Kodithuwakku concludes his distinguished service at the University of Peradeniya, his career offers a compelling reminder that academic leadership is ultimately about more than personal accomplishment. It is about building institutions, challenging established thinking and creating opportunities that endure.

While his formal academic career comes to a close, the programs, institutions and generations of students shaped by his contribution ensure that his influence will continue well beyond the lecture halls of Peradeniya.

title: Cabinet backs mandatory Sri Lanka Standards for imported car and three-wheeler tyres | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 23 October 2026 04:48
-     - 285

The Cabinet of Ministers has approved submitting new regulations to Parliament requiring imported passenger car tyres and three-wheeler pneumatic tyres to meet Sri Lanka Standards (SLS), in a move aimed at protecting local manufacturers and consumers.

“The Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Ministry recommended introducing import testing methods under SLS for the two categories of tyres, citing the need to ensure a fair competitive environment for local manufacturers and to safeguard consumer safety and security,” Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said at the weekly post-Cabinet meeting media briefing this week.

Acting on the recommendation, the Imports and Exports (Control) Regulations, No. 08 of 2026, were enacted through Extraordinary Gazette Notification No. 2508/27 dated 1 October 2026, amending the regulations currently in force.

He said as per the amended rules, imported passenger car tyres (HS Code 4011.10.90) must comply with SLS 1212, while imported pneumatic tyres for three-wheeled vehicles (HS Code 4011.90.10) must comply with SLS 1347.

The proposal to this effect was submitted by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, in his capacity as the Finance, Planning and Economic Development Minister.
